skill.name: ai-code-cleanup
skill.description: Remove AI-generated artifacts from code branches after AI-assisted coding sessions. The skill focuses on redundant comments, defensive bloat, unnecessary type casts, style drift, and safe verification.
skill.summary: Cleans AI-generated code artifacts while preserving behavior and project style.
skill.author: Joseph OBrien

content.value_statement: AI coding sessions can leave redundant comments, defensive checks, type casts, and inconsistent style. This skill guides focused cleanup that preserves behavior and verifies changes.
actual_capabilities: Identifies redundant comments that restate obvious code.
Flags unnecessary defensive checks on trusted paths.
Finds avoidable type casts and TypeScript ignore comments.
Checks naming, formatting, imports, and declarations against local style.
Guides surgical edits that reduce code while preserving behavior.
Encourages compile, test, and regression checks after cleanup.
limitations: It cannot prove behavior preservation without project tests or runtime checks.
It depends on clear project conventions to judge style accurately.
It may need human review before removing defensive code on untrusted inputs.
It does not replace security review or performance profiling.

use_cases.title: Prepare an AI-Assisted Branch
use_cases.description: Review changed files for redundant comments, type workarounds, and defensive bloat before opening a pull request.

use_cases.title: Reduce Review Noise
use_cases.description: Clean style drift and obvious generated artifacts so reviewers can focus on behavior and architecture.

use_cases.title: Standardize Generated Contributions
use_cases.description: Apply project cleanup rules to code produced by different assistants before merging into the main branch.

prompt_templates.title: Clean a Branch
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner cleanup after an AI coding session
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this branch for AI-generated code artifacts. Remove redundant comments, unnecessary defensive checks, type workarounds, and style inconsistencies. Preserve behavior and tell me what changed.

prompt_templates.title: Clean Specific Files
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused cleanup for a known area
prompt_templates.prompt: Clean the files I changed in src/. Match the existing project style, keep useful comments, and remove only code that does not affect behavior. Run available checks when finished.

prompt_templates.title: Review Before Pull Request
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare this branch with main and identify AI-generated artifacts in the changed files. Make small cleanup edits, list removed patterns, and confirm the tests or checks you ran.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Risky Cleanup
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a cleanup plan for generated code in this module before editing. Separate safe removals from changes that need tests or reviewer approval. Then apply only the safe edits first.

output_examples.input: Remove unnecessary comments from an authentication utility.
output: Reports that redundant comments were removed while useful context was kept.
Shows that line count decreased and behavior stayed the same.
Notes which tests or checks passed after the cleanup.

output_examples.input: Clean defensive bloat from a user API helper.
output: Identifies redundant validation already handled by callers.
Keeps legitimate error handling for database failures and untrusted inputs.
Summarizes the reduced code path and remaining risks for review.

output_examples.input: Prepare an AI-generated pull request for review.
output: Groups cleanup by comments, type workarounds, style drift, and defensive checks.
Lists files changed and explains why each edit is safe.
Flags any cleanup that needs reviewer judgment instead of applying it.

best_practices: Run the skill on a small diff and review each edit before merging.
Keep defensive checks for untrusted input, external data, and security boundaries.
Verify cleanup with the project formatter, type checker, and test suite when available.
anti_patterns: Do not remove comments that explain business rules, security decisions, or non-obvious behavior.
Do not simplify code only because it looks verbose without checking callers and tests.
Do not apply cleanup across unrelated files in one large change.

faq.question: Does this skill change code automatically?
faq.answer: It guides cleanup edits when used by an agent. You should review the diff before merging.

faq.question: Can it remove real error handling by mistake?
faq.answer: Yes, if context is unclear. Keep error handling for untrusted input, external services, and security boundaries.

faq.question: Does it work with TypeScript projects?
faq.answer: Yes. It specifically looks for unnecessary casts, ignore comments, and type workarounds.

faq.question: Should I run tests after cleanup?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill expects compile, type, lint, or test checks whenever the project supports them.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is this a replacement for code review?
faq.answer: No. It prepares a cleaner diff, but reviewers still need to check behavior and architecture.
